title: A sleep cycle restarts about every 80 to 100 minutes
summary: NHLBI says a person cycles through REM and non-REM, the cycle starts over every 80 to 100 minutes, and a night usually has four to six cycles.
body: The stages page says the cycle of REM and non-REM starts over every 80 to 100 minutes. A night usually has four to six of those cycles. A person may wake briefly between cycles. That timing is the pattern NHLBI prints for a usual night. It is not a promise that a baby, or a sick person, will show the same spacing.

sources.title: How Sleep Works: Sleep Phases and Stages
sources.author: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Supports the stage or REM sentence named in the card. Page last updated 24 March 2022.
